payload.answer:
Based on the NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust Architecture specification, the Policy Engine (PE), Policy Administrator (PA), and Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) interact through the following flow before granting enclave access:

1. **Policy Engine (PE) to Policy Administrator (PA) [Control Plane]:** The PE evaluates continuous device posture, BeyondCorp context-aware access levels, and Chronicle threat intelligence feeds (`02_Zero_Trust_Architecture_Specs.pdf`, p. 1). Based on this evaluation, the PE signals the PA to mint short-lived mTLS / OIDC session tokens (`02_Zero_Trust_Architecture_Specs.pdf`, p. 1).
2. **Policy Administrator (PA) to Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) [Data Plane]:** The PEP—which consists of Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) and Envoy Service Mesh ingress gateways—terminates all untrusted traffic from the untrusted subject and device (`02_Zero_Trust_Architecture_Specs.pdf`, p. 1). The PEP then permits per-request access to the protected enterprise enclave resources *only* upon verification by the PA (`02_Zero_Trust_Architecture_Specs.pdf`, p. 1). 
3. **Continuous Telemetry:** Every allow or deny decision made by the PEP is subsequently streamed to the Google SecOps SIEM (`02_Zero_Trust_Architecture_Specs.pdf`, p. 1).

payload.rationale: Every claim in the candidate answer (PE evaluation inputs, PA minting mTLS/OIDC tokens, PEP via IAP and Envoy gateways permitting per-request access only on PA verification, telemetry to Google SecOps SIEM) maps directly to the ZTA exhibit, and the answer fully matches the reference. Only the ZTA exhibit chunk is truly relevant. The SEC-03 RFP and SLA chunks are marginally related, and the rest (CLOUD-01, DATA-02, Bank of America, Elephant Talk) are off-topic noise, which yields low precision.

payload.answer:
Based on the NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust Architecture specification, the Policy Engine (PE), Policy Administrator (PA), and Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) interact through the following flow before granting enclave access:

1. **Policy Engine (PE) to Policy Administrator (PA) [Control Plane]:** The PE evaluates continuous device posture, BeyondCorp context-aware access levels, and Chronicle threat intelligence feeds (`02_Zero_Trust_Architecture_Specs.pdf`, p. 1). Based on this evaluation, the PE signals the PA to mint short-lived mTLS / OIDC session tokens (`02_Zero_Trust_Architecture_Specs.pdf`, p. 1).
2. **Policy Administrator (PA) to Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) [Data Plane]:** The PEP—which consists of Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) and Envoy Service Mesh ingress gateways—terminates all untrusted traffic from the untrusted subject and device (`02_Zero_Trust_Architecture_Specs.pdf`, p. 1). The PEP then permits per-request access to the protected enterprise enclave resources *only* upon verification by the PA (`02_Zero_Trust_Architecture_Specs.pdf`, p. 1). 
3. **Continuous Telemetry:** Every allow or deny decision made by the PEP is subsequently streamed to the Google SecOps SIEM (`02_Zero_Trust_Architecture_Specs.pdf`, p. 1).

evaluation.rationale: Every claim in the candidate answer (PE evaluation inputs, PA minting mTLS/OIDC tokens, PEP via IAP and Envoy gateways permitting per-request access only on PA verification, telemetry to Google SecOps SIEM) maps directly to the ZTA exhibit, and the answer fully matches the reference. Only the ZTA exhibit chunk is truly relevant. The SEC-03 RFP and SLA chunks are marginally related, and the rest (CLOUD-01, DATA-02, Bank of America, Elephant Talk) are off-topic noise, which yields low precision.
